note: Button Link is a single field formatter plugin (ButtonLinkFormatter, id 'button_link', label 'Link as Button') for core Link fields, extending core LinkFormatter. It has NO configure route, no settings form, no permissions, no Drush, no config schema, no plugin types. Its only persistent state is the formatter's per-field, per-view-mode settings inside an entity_view_display config entity: content.<field>.type=button_link plus settings.btn_type/btn_size/btn_block/link_text/additional_class/icon_class/disable_btn_role. Bootstrap CSS is not bundled. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real view-display config: introspection reads back which link field uses the button formatter and its btn_type/icon; execution switches a link field's formatter to button_link and sets its options, verified against the live entity_view_display.

evals.prompt: I have a Link field on my Drupal 11 Article content type and I want it to render as a Bootstrap button using the button_link module. What is the formatter called, which field type does it apply to, and where do I select it?
evals.expected_output: Use the 'Link as Button' formatter (id button_link), which applies to core 'link' fields. Select it on the entity's Manage display page for the Link field, then set button type/size/etc.

evals.prompt: In the button_link 'Link as Button' formatter, which setting controls the button colour/style and what are the available options? Does the module ship the Bootstrap CSS?
evals.expected_output: The btn_type setting controls the style: btn-default (default), btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-success, btn-info, btn-warning, btn-danger, btn-light, btn-dark, btn-link. The module does NOT ship Bootstrap CSS; your theme must provide the .btn styles.

evals.prompt: Using the button_link module's Link as Button formatter, how do I add an icon (e.g. a Font Awesome icon) before the button label, and which template renders the output?
evals.expected_output: Set the icon_class setting (e.g. 'fa fa-anchor'); it is rendered as a leading inside the anchor by the link_formatter_button_link theme hook / link-formatter-button-link.html.twig template.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a Link field field_btl_known whose display is configured with the button_link module. Inspect the live default view display for Article and tell me which Bootstrap button type (btn_type) it uses.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_btl_known component uses type button_link with settings.btn_type = btn-success. Read via drush cget core.entity_view_display.node.article.default content.field_btl_known.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has a Link field field_btl_icon rendered as a button by the button_link module, and it is configured to show an icon. Inspect the live display configuration and state the exact icon CSS class that is set.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_btl_icon component (type button_link) has settings.icon_class = 'fa fa-anchor'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a Link field field_btl_task that currently uses the default link formatter. Using the button_link module, change its display on the default view mode so it renders as a Bootstrap PRIMARY button (btn_type = btn-primary). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_btl_task component has type=button_link and settings.btn_type=btn-primary (set via Manage display or setComponent).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article Link field field_btl_task2 currently uses the default link formatter. Use the button_link module to display it as a LARGE button (btn_size = btn-lg) with a leading icon whose class is exactly 'fa fa-star'. Apply the change to the live default view display.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_btl_task2 component has type=button_link with settings.btn_size=btn-lg and settings.icon_class='fa fa-star'.
